beatOutlines.textOutline: At 9:30 AM, Raju smiles seeing a green candle on his screen.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji glances at the chart and cautions him immediately.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Ignoring the warning, Raju places a buy order at ₹420.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju bought at ₹420 right after an extended multi-day rally.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: By afternoon, aggressive selling dragged the price down to ₹380.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's rule is clear: candle identity is dictated by preceding trend and location.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Candlestick analysis starts with the foundational anatomy of real bodies and shadows.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The second stage identifies single-candle turning points: Doji, Hammer, and Hanging Man.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The third stage decodes high-probability multi-candle reversal formations.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: And finally, filtering false signals by pairing patterns with Western indicators.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The real body represents the decisive battle between open and close.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: While shadows or wicks expose the price extremes rejected by market consensus.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: When both sides match perfectly, a Doji forms: the quintessential state of market indecision.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: During an uptrend, aggressive buyers dominate order flow.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: At the top, a Doji marks parity between buyers and sellers.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy stresses: Doji is not an automatic short; it's a caution flag that trend inertia is fading.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Hammer and Hanging Man share identical visual shape, yet their implications are exact opposites.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The Hanging Man at tops warns that bears possess enough ammunition to trigger sharp intraday breaks.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Never act on a Hanging Man alone: confirmation via a lower close the next session is mandatory.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: In a Bullish Engulfing pattern, a massive green real body entirely swallows the previous red body.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Conversely, a Bearish Engulfing at resistance marks decisive surrender by buyers.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's guideline: larger engulfed-to-engulfing size ratios indicate higher institutional impact.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dark Cloud Cover strikes uptrend tops when prices gap to new highs then plunge.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The Piercing Line is its bottom counterpart: gapping down below the red candle, then closing past the 50% midpoint.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: If the close fails to pierce the 50% midpoint, Japanese chartists discard it as incomplete.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Morning Star is a 3-candle bottom reversal: long red candle, small star body, and a surging green candle.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Evening Star crowns the top, where a large red candle following the star confirms the bear trend.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Murphy's biggest lesson: filtered candle patterns combined with moving averages slash false whipsaws.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Now it's your turn. Examine this scenario carefully.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Think... focus on the prior trend direction and candle location.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: It is a Hanging Man, not a Hammer! After an extended rally, this pattern warns of imminent bearish reversal.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: At market close, Raju opens his trading journal with a valuable realization.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Sharma ji smiles and slides over a cup of hot cutting chai.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Raju writes down: Trend dictates the name, confirmation validates the trade.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: The real body captures open-close consensus, while shadows mark intraday rejected extremes.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Doji marks complete indecision, and Hammer vs Hanging Man identity is governed purely by trend location.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Never trade Hanging Man unconfirmed, and Engulfing patterns demand complete body-over-body coverage.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Dark Cloud Cover and Piercing Line strictly mandate closing past the prior body's 50% midpoint.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Morning and Evening Stars deliver 3-day macro reversal confirmations, while Western filters weed out false traps.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

beatOutlines.textOutline: Remember the ultimate takeaway: location defines the pattern, and Western indicators confirm the trigger.
beatOutlines.speaker: narrator

summarySteps: Real Body vs Shadows: Open-close conviction vs intraday price rejection
Doji: Zero body marks deadlock and trend fatigue
Hammer vs Hanging Man: Same shape, opposite meanings based on trend location
Confirmation Rule: Hanging Man always requires lower close confirmation
Engulfing Patterns: Bullish and Bearish bodies totally swallow previous session
Dark Cloud & Piercing: Mandatory 50% midpoint body penetration test
Morning & Evening Stars: Three-candle high-conviction reversal setups
Filtered Confluence: Combine Japanese candles with Western indicators & support
bottomTakeaway: Discipline and grounded market understanding are essential for survival.
